svg.title: Jing-Zhang Resonance Loop: Four Review Handoff Cards
svg.desc: Movement, rights, human takeover and everyday-care cards turn the three anchors' spatial actions into verifiable civic benefits, responsibility interfaces and exit responses.
svg.text: Jing-Zhang Resonance Loop | Four Review Handoff Cards
From concept drawing to reversible pilot: every AI service leaves a civic benefit, accountable interface and exit response
The three anchors do not expand directly; each action passes these four review cards first

g.text: 01 | Movement card
Check first: route, crossing, access, shade and night legibility
Leave: physical map, ground cues, rest point and staffed inquiry
Accountable: park/street operations + access specialists
If not: correct the route before adding digital service
02 | Rights card
Check first: consent, attribution and usable withdrawal
Leave: consent notice, withdrawal route and staffed advice
Accountable: university transfer + open source + IP services
If not: remove or do not publish; a pilot never bypasses rights
03 | Human-takeover card
Check first: whether a person can take over an incident
Leave: staffed desk, stop condition and revision digest
Accountable: scenario operator + on-site safety role
If not: reduce scope, turn prompts off, retain static information
04 | Everyday-care card
Check first: whether care works in rain, night and peaks
Leave: care card, offline reporting route and review date
Accountable: landscape/facility/merchant or venue maintainer
If not: remove temporary elements; restore routine care first
